legend: Given two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$. An array a$$$a$$$ is considered good if the following conditions hold:
The length of a$$$a$$$ is equal to n$$$n$$$.
The sum of elements of a$$$a$$$ is equal to k$$$k$$$ (i.e. ∑ai=k$$$\sum a_i = k$$$).

The cost of the array a$$$a$$$ is equal to the sum of ai$$$a_i$$$ &$$$\&$$$ ai−1$$$a_{i - 1}$$$ for all i$$$i$$$ such that 1<i≤n$$$1  \lt  i \le n$$$, where &$$$\&$$$ is the bitwise AND[9]$$$^{[9]}$$$ operator.
Your task is to find the minimum cost of a good array.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤5000$$$1 \le t \le 5000$$$) — the number of test cases.
Each line of the following t$$$t$$$ lines of the input consists of two space-separated integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤n≤106,n≤k≤109$$$1 \le n \le 10^6, n \le k \le 10^9$$$).
Notice that there is no limit on the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all the test cases.
output: Output t$$$t$$$ lines, the i$$$i$$$-th of which contains a single integer — the minimum cost of a good array in the i$$$i$$$-th testcase.
